title: Randomized verifier characterization
statement: Let $p:\bbn\to\bbq$ and let $L$ be a language of Boolean strings. There exist a Boolean-valued verifier $M(x,r)$ and natural numbers $a,k$ such that the verifier runs in polynomial time, every $x\in L$ is accepted with probability at least $p(|x|)$ when given a uniformly random Boolean string of length $\mathrm{polyLen}(a,k,|x|)$, and every $x\notin L$ is rejected for every Boolean string of that length.
hypotheses_covered: Existence of a Boolean-valued verifier on pairs of Boolean strings
The verifier's option-valued computation runs in polynomial time
For every member $x\in L$, acceptance probability is at least $p(|x|)$ using the specified random-string length
For every nonmember $x\notin L$, rejection holds for every Boolean string of the specified length
